title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #221
gist: Packy McCormick's Thanksgiving Dose catalogs a week of claimed breakthroughs: Levent Alpöge and an unreleased Claude producing a Lean-verified proof of the (Generalized) Riemann Hypothesis, AI-assisted quantum-gravity work, an FCC authorization for SpaceX's 1M-satellite orbital data-center constellation, Neuralink's pivotal trial, Senate passage of the BAAJA permitting reform, Hadrian's SF factory, and the first patient living a year with a pig kidney.

insights.claim: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge released a 17-million-line Lean formal proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, developed over six weeks with an unreleased frontier version of Claude.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Frontier labs' AI can now produce verified results on century-old problems — a step-change signal for AI capability valuations.
insights.locator: (1) Alpöge & Claude Prove

insights.claim: Within 24 hours the Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative certified both the theorem statement and Alpöge's proof as valid after independent formally verified proof checkers ran it.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Machine verification lets AI-generated results be trusted at speed — formal verification tools gain strategic importance.
insights.quote: We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct.
insights.locator: Within 24 hours, on Saturday afternoon

insights.claim: No human can yet read Alpöge's Riemann proof: there is no natural-language paper, only machine-verified code, which Terence Tao said appears to draw on the full power of the Langlands program and arithmetic geometry.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: 'Centaur math' — verification precedes human understanding; a new paradigm for AI-assisted research.
insights.locator: There was a bit of controversy

insights.claim: Steven Strogatz described the Alpöge–Claude collaboration as an AI jockey riding a fast AI horse, which McCormick labels 'Centaur Math.'
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Human+AI pairing is the productive unit in frontier research.
insights.quote: a very skilled AI jockey riding a very fast AI horse.
insights.locator: Steven Strogatz called the duo

insights.claim: Both Anthropic and OpenAI posted AI-generated proofs of VP ≠ VNP, the algebraic cousin of P vs NP, and McCormick relays rumors the labs may have cracked P vs NP too — which could invalidate much cryptography if P = NP.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Rumor-level but tail risk to cryptographic assumptions (crypto assets, security vendors) worth monitoring.
insights.locator: Oh, and both Anthropic and OpenAI

insights.claim: OpenAI's Ven Chandrasekaran proposed an AI-assisted, background-independent quantization of vacuum general relativity in 4D that recovers Bekenstein-Hawking entropy and semiclassical Einstein equations, though it covers only vacuum and still needs peer checking.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Another datapoint of AI accelerating frontier science; not yet a Theory of Everything.
insights.locator: lol. It’s Thanksgiving week

insights.claim: Elon Musk said every US child will receive two SpaceX shares (one from SpaceX, one from him), plus one more per child per year from him, via Trump Accounts.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Broadens retail ownership of SpaceX; Trump Accounts become a distribution channel for private equity.
insights.locator: SpaceX and Elon are Giving Every American Kid

insights.claim: McCormick estimates that with ~6.4B shares controlled by Musk and ~72M US kids, Musk's annual share gifts would transfer more than 10% of his SpaceX ownership to American children within a decade.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Gradual dilution of Musk's personal SpaceX stake via gifting.
insights.locator: He currently controls about 6.4 billion shares

insights.claim: The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites for its Starmind orbital data-center constellation — the first US authorization for a constellation of data centers in space.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Regulatory green light for space-based compute; execution hinges on building satellites and Starship cadence.
insights.locator: FCC Authorizes SpaceX to Deploy 1 Million

insights.claim: McCormick states Starship became fully reusable last week, which is the launch capability SpaceX needs to send up a million data-center satellites.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Reusable heavy lift is the cost unlock behind orbital compute economics.
insights.locator: Now they just have to make a million DC satellites

insights.claim: The FDA approved Neuralink's LINK study, described as the first US pivotal trial for an implantable brain-computer interface, with ALS patients potentially eligible.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: BCI moves to pivotal-trial stage — commercialization path for neurotech is opening.
insights.locator: Neuralink Gets FDA Approval to Launch LINK

insights.claim: The US Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA, H.R. 2347) 62–33, streamlining NEPA, Clean Water Act and Endangered Species Act reviews; it now goes to the House.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: If enacted, faster permitting is a tailwind for transmission, nuclear, energy and data-center developers.
insights.locator: (2) U.S. Senate Passes Bipartisan Permitting Reform

insights.claim: BAAJA includes dedicated provisions to accelerate electric transmission lines, nuclear licensing, energy permitting broadly and data-center projects.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Directly relevant to grid, nuclear and AI-infrastructure equities.
insights.locator: It includes dedicated provisions

insights.claim: McCormick argues scientific and energy breakthroughs are wasted if turning them into physical infrastructure takes a decade, making permitting the binding constraint on progress.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Physical deployment speed, not invention, is the bottleneck — favour builders that benefit from reform.
insights.locator: We can make all of the breakthroughs we want

insights.claim: Hadrian, a Not Boring Capital portfolio company, plans to open a 1 million sq ft development factory and engineering campus in San Francisco in January, after raising $1.37B at a $7.87B valuation.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Reshoring/defense-manufacturing startups command large valuations; AI-enabled factories locating near AI talent. (Author has a conflict: portfolio company.)
insights.locator: (3) Hadrian is Opening a Factory

insights.claim: Hadrian pairs humans with AI-enabled software to automate precision-parts manufacturing and capture tribal knowledge from skilled workers.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Human-in-the-loop automation is the model for reindustrialization plays.
insights.locator: AI (or SI, whatever) helps them automate

insights.claim: Capable, founded by Isaak Freeman, emerged from stealth with a vertically integrated, AI-enabled autonomous preclinical lab, starting with peptides and aiming at endurance, longevity, less sleep and stronger bones.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Early-stage AI x bio; vertical integration (run experiments, generate data) is the thesis — no results yet.
insights.locator: (4) Capable Comes Out of Stealth

insights.claim: Molly Falco became the first person to live a full year off dialysis with a genetically engineered pig kidney from eGenesis carrying 69 edits, transplanted at Massachusetts General Hospital.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Xenotransplantation crossing durability milestones de-risks the field.
insights.locator: (5) Patient Marks One Year Living With Pig Kidney

insights.claim: Of six pig-kidney recipients since 2024, three currently have functioning organs; eGenesis will launch formal trials in 33 patients in Q1 next year, and United Therapeutics performed its first pig thymo-kidney transplant and has FDA clearance for a pig heart trial.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: United Therapeutics (UTHR) is the listed exposure to xenotransplant progress; competitive field forming.
insights.locator: The pig kidney transplants are going to keep going

insights.claim: More than 500,000 Americans rely on dialysis (five-year mortality ~55%), with over 90,000 on the kidney waitlist and twelve dying daily awaiting a kidney — the addressable need for xenotransplants.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Large TAM; successful xenotransplants threaten the dialysis business model long-term.
insights.locator: More than 500,000 Americans rely on dialysis
